statement: Assume the preceding spectral and noise diagnostics, the zero-field approximate-root exclusion in Lemma 17.3, the field representation (17.7), and |PW t h|n ≥ ct5/4. The test (17.2) holds with positive fixed slack; in particular Fh has a unique root y∗(h). At all roots of Fh, and with arbitrarily small additional errors at sufficiently accurate approximate roots, set z = r + r−1 , R = (z − W)−1 . For sufficiently small fixed t and then sufficiently large n, q ≥ c √ t, |y − r−1 Rh|n = o( √ q), KTAP = R − 4q RyyTR/n 1 + 4q⟨yRy⟩ + o(q−2 ). (17.13) Here KTAP = ∂h tanh y∗(h), and the last error is in operator norm. The errors tend to zero as the boundary scales decrease, after which all dimensional errors and perturbation tolerances are chosen. If q is comparable to √ t, define the TAP potential per site by T (h) = ⟨hm⟩ + 1 2⟨mWm⟩ − ⟨I(m)⟩ + 1 4r2 , I(v) = 1 2(1 + v) log(1 + v) + 1 2(1 − v) log(1 − v). With κ0 = 1/3, the value expansion is T (h) − 1 2⟨hRh⟩ = r2 4 + zq 2 − ⟨I(m)⟩ − ⟨eRe⟩ 2r2 = 1 4 + κ0q3 + o(q3 ), e = tanh y − ry. (17.14) All assertions persist to any prescribed small macroscopic error under sufficiently small changes of the interaction coefficient, operator-norm perturbations, and normalized field displacements, with the TAP potential using the actual interaction and jr2/4 at its actual root.
